title: Case-distinct JSON keys colliding under a case-insensitive parser are detected
question_or_target: Do two keys differing only in case produce a detected collision rather than last-key-wins? PASS requires our emitter to never produce case-colliding keys AND our validator to reject an incoming document that has them.

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer verified the artifact at command-center/receipts/TST-0180.json exists on disk (25727 LF-normalized bytes), parses as JSON, carried the builder terminal state=BLOCKED with failure.classification=[reviewer-absent] and reviewer=null (no self-certification) at review time, and its report.kind=parser_report matches the catalog output_schema pin.

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer re-ran both named probes live for 3 rounds each under the ambient environment; all exited 0 with the unit SUCCESS sentinel (probe1_case_collision.py=3/3 rounds rc0; probe2_folded_set_size.py=3/3 rounds rc0); live sentinels match the builder-recorded raw_output lines (consistent=True).

probes.raw_output: SUCCESS:TST-0180-probe1 distinct=valid collision=rejected named=['hooks', 'Hooks'] | SUCCESS:TST-0180-probe2 fold_delta=2 emitter_clean=True last_wins=True
